speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether having a mental health-related condition is a ground for being ineligible for the Home Protection Scheme (HPS); (b) if so, what is the rationale; and (c) what specific mental health-related conditions will prevent the take-up of HPS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members of the House, this is in line with industry practice.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This ensures the affordability of premiums for the majority of members as well as the viability of the scheme.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I think different types of conditions may have different implications in terms of behaviour and in terms of the propensity to do different things that could affect the actuarial basis of the scheme.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, just wanted to confirm the understanding that you would be looking at severity as well as the type of mental health conditions to decide on eligibility.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we do take a nuanced approach, but it is based on advice from experts and medical experts, including psychiatric experts, if you talk about mental illness.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because you can imagine and you can surmise or conclude that if you disclose it after the event and you have a pre-existing condition that you do not disclose upfront and if something then happens, after that for you to then go back and have all that data, I think it would be very difficult for us to access that data.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, the approach is a very balanced, very measured and a calibrated one.
